text:
eva: Quick follow-up to yesterday's batcher RFC — sketching an 'admission gateway' idea for continuous batching. I'm worried about credit leakage vs KV-cache eviction interactions. Can we sync?

nick: yep, curious about the flow and failure modes.

eva: sketch: incoming req -> admission gateway (token check) -> fast-batcher path if token ok else slow-path queue. tokens refill per-tenant + global borrow fallbacks. slow-path gets deprioritized on KV misses.

raj: tokens-per-request needs to account for request size + model seq len. otherwise tiny requests vs large streams will unfairly map.

sophia: +1. also: how do we handle preemption? stealing tokens from in-flight batches could break long-running streaming.

liam: idea: add 'urgency' flag. small RPCs get ephemeral tokens on the fast path; streaming/large jobs require reservations. Also want metrics: token_usage, borrow_events, kv_miss_penalty.

eva: proposed telemetry names: batcher.admission.tokens_allocated, batcher.admission.tokens_borrowed, batcher.admission.kv_misses, batcher.admission.slowpath_enqueue_count. tag by tenant_id, pool (dedicated/hosted).

nick: edge-case: noisy small-requests flood — need cooldown and a short-term blackhole detector. maybe enforcement by sliding-window p99 rather than pure token count.

sophia: and dedicated tenants must get guaranteed tokens; private customers shouldn't be starved by multi-tenant burst borrow.

raj: implementation question: should the gateway live in front of the scheduler (LB-level) or inside admission in the scheduler service? front-of-scheduler short-circuits expensive ops but duplicates logic on hosts.

eva: tradeoffs: host-level gateway -> cheap short-circuit, but inconsistent counters; central admission service -> single source of truth, easier to enforce borrowing rules, more RPCs. leaning central + sharded counters.

scheduler-bot: Reminder: current admission API endpoints: POST /admit (stateless), POST /reserve. Adding token semantics requires a small schema bump and rate-limit review.

liam: proto sketch (very small):
```proto
message AdmitRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  int32 token_cost = 2; // default 1
  bool urgency = 3;
  repeated int32 seq_lengths = 4;
}
```

sophia: keep token_cost default=1 for backwards compat. we can autotune token_cost based on seq_length histogram later.

nick: experiment plan: canary in one region. initial token_cost=1, urgent=small reqs 0.5. run 48h, compare p50/p99 latency and cost.

eva: I'll own the canary. rollout checklist: dashboards (token allocation, borrow rate), alerts (borrow > 5/min, kv_miss spike), rollback path to disable gateway.

sophia: add alert for slow-path-latency > 2x baseline.

raj: perf note: centralizing counters means we must be careful about RPC hot spots. sharding by tenant hash + local caches + occasional reconciliation.

liam: for fairness, implement token caps + slow replenishment window for tenants that over-borrow repeatedly.

nick: docs + runtime config update required. Who will PR?

eva: I will draft the RFC follow-up doc with concrete metrics and canary steps. Link when ready.

eva: placeholder doc: https://docs.google.com/xxx :spiral_note_pad:

sophia: :thumbsup:

nick: thanks — will review the doc when posted.

raj: one more thought: tie KV-cache eviction hints to admission decisions — if a tenant is causing high KV churn, increase their token cost temporarily.

eva: good idea. we'll add kv_eviction_penalty to the scoring function.

liam: ok, sounds like a plan. thanks all.

sophia: +1
